item.title: Liangzhu forum opens, highlights heritage conservation, int'l cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Lina Mendoni, Minister of Culture of Greece, addresses the opening ceremony of the fourth Liangzhu Forum in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province, Oct. 18, 2026. The fourth Liangzhu Forum opened Sunday in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province, to discuss challenges in cultural heritage conservation and paths to deepen international cooperation. The year 2026 marks the 90th anniversary of the discovery of the Liangzhu ruins. Themed "Bridging the Past and the Future: Safeguarding Cultural Heritage for Our Times," the forum brings together officials, archaeologists and scholars from around the world. (Xinhua/Xu Yu)
HANGZHOU, Oct. 18 (Xinhua) -- The fourth Liangzhu Forum opened Sunday in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province, to discuss challenges in cultural heritage conservation and paths to deepen international cooperation.
Experts and scholars will discuss topics ranging from early civilizations to archaeological research on ancient cities, with new research findings and advances also set to be unveiled, Zhang Ling, an official with China's National Cultural Heritage Administration, said at an earlier briefing.
Participants will address challenges including the loss of cultural heritage, advances in technologies for protecting and utilizing cultural relics, and sustainable tourism, Zhang added.
Lina Mendoni, Minister of Culture of Greece, said in a speech at the opening ceremony that people must move beyond traditional approaches and adopt adaptive, preventive and holistic management to safeguard cultural heritage.
"UNESCO believes that sustainable tourism can help safeguard cultural heritage by raising awareness of the importance of heritage for future generations, improving cultural understanding and strengthening local livelihoods," said Nayef Al-Fayez, UNESCO Assistant Director-General for Culture, in his video speech.
The forum brings together four international organizations: UNESCO, based in Paris; the International Centre for the Study of the Preservation and Restoration of Cultural Property, headquartered in Rome; the Alliance for Cultural Heritage in Asia, based in Beijing; and the International Alliance for the Protection of Heritage, headquartered in Geneva.
The gathering marks a step for the forum to turn into a broader venue for multilateral dialogue on cultural heritage, said Wen Dayan, another official with the National Cultural Heritage Administration.
This year's event includes an opening ceremony and main forum, five sub-forums and five companion events, including an international artists' creative tour exhibition, a Liangzhu cultural and creative market, a design exhibition and international dialogues.
Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2019, the Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City offer important evidence of an early regional state that flourished more than 5,000 years ago.
The inaugural forum was held in Hangzhou in 2023. The fourth edition runs through Tuesday and is co-hosted by China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism, the National Cultural Heritage Administration and the Zhejiang provincial government.

item.title: China railway passenger trips hit record high in first three quarters
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Passengers are seen at Harbin Railway Station in Harbin, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, Oct. 7, 2026. (Photo by Yuan Yong/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Oct. 18 (Xinhua) -- China's railway network handled 3.71 billion passenger trips in the first three quarters of 2026, up 4.8 percent year on year, the highest for the period, according to the China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway).
During the period, the railway network operated an average of 11,511 passenger trains daily, up 5.3 percent from a year earlier.
Railway departments have actively responded to demand for sightseeing, wellness tours and red-themed study tours, according to China Railway. In the first nine months, a total of 2,860 tourist trains were operated across the country, up 25.5 percent year on year.
The railway network also operated 947 special trains for concertgoers and sports fans during the period, effectively boosting the catering, hotel and cultural tourism sectors.
Cross-border rail travel also continued to grow. The China-Laos Railway carried 265,000 cross-border trips, up 37.8 percent, while the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong high-speed railway handled over 25.8 million cross-border trips, up 11.8 percent, China Railway said.
China Railway also adapted to the inbound travel boom created by the country's visa-free transit policy. The railway network carried over 19 million foreign passenger trips in the first three quarters, up 33.4 percent year on year, the company said.
Behind the steady growth in passenger traffic is China's increasingly dense high-speed rail network.
By the end of 2025, the country's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, which included more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail.
On Sept. 28, China opened four high-speed rail sections, connecting Xiongan in north China's Hebei Province with Shangqiu in Henan Province in central China, Xi'an with Ankang in Shaanxi Province in northwest China, Yichang with Xingshan in central China's Hubei Province, and Harbin with Yichun in Heilongjiang Province in the country's northeast.
China's high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, featuring eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. Once complete, the network will connect major cities, city clusters and key economic zones across the country.

item.title: Iran's IRGC says 2nd supertanker explodes after hitting mine in Hormuz Strait
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18
TEHRAN, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- The navy of Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) announced Saturday that a second "violating" supertanker had exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine, hours after a similar incident involving another tanker.
In a statement published on the IRGC's official news outlet Sepah News, the navy said the blast occurred on Saturday morning, causing a "huge" fire on the vessel, which was carrying over 2 million barrels of crude oil.
It said the oil tanker had turned off its GPS and radar systems and was seeking to cross the waterway through an "illegal" route, adding that the explosion occurred in the vessel's engine room and brought it to a halt.
Earlier in the day, the IRGC Navy said another "violating" supertanker seeking to transit the strait through an "unauthorized" route had suffered a "huge" explosion after hitting a naval mine.
It added that the explosion resulted in a "massive" fire on the oil tanker, which had turned off its GPS and radar systems and was carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil.
Iran tightened its grip on the Strait of Hormuz on Feb. 28, barring safe passage of vessels belonging to or affiliated with Israel and the United States following their joint strikes on Iranian territory.

item.title: "China Magnet" attracts growing interest from global talent
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18
A foreign tourist tries on hair ornaments at a mall in Shanghai, east China, May 5, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Haoming)
* A growing number of foreign professionals are drawn to China by its expanding career opportunities, as the country's fast-growing industries strengthen its appeal amid economic pressures in some overseas markets. Positive experiences shared by foreign visitors on social media are also helping improve global perceptions of China.
* China's emerging industries, from artificial intelligence and robotics to new energy, are strengthening the pull of innovation, offering international professionals opportunities to put their expertise into practice.
* As Chinese technology companies expand globally, their growing demand for international expertise is creating career opportunities beyond China's borders.
BEIJING, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- For 33-year-old Federico Flamenco, a Salvadoran engineer working in China's robotics industry, a once-distant career dream has become a reality.
"Working in robotics is something I could once only dream about. Now I work with robotic arms and get to see how quickly humanoid robots are developing here in China," he said.
After earning a bachelor's degree in El Salvador, Flamenco pursued a master's degree in electrical engineering in China. Currently at JAKA Robotics, a Chinese robotics company, he helps overseas customers find suitable robotic solutions, drawing on his engineering expertise and knowledge of Spanish, English, Chinese and Portuguese.
This undated photo shows Salvadoran engineer Federico Flamenco working at robotics company JAKA Robotics in Shanghai, east China. (Xinhua)
Flamenco is among a growing number of foreign professionals drawn to China by expanding career opportunities, as its fast-growing industries strengthen the country's appeal amid economic pressures in some overseas markets. Positive experiences shared by foreign visitors on social media are also helping improve perceptions of China abroad.
CHINA ON THE RADAR
Miriam Wickertsheim, general manager of Direct HR, a recruitment firm that helps international companies in China hire senior executives, has seen the shift firsthand.
"Global interest in working in China has more than doubled this year compared with two years ago, with a major surge in inquiries in early summer," said Wickertsheim.
"We receive numerous inquiries from jobseekers in Europe, Australia, Arab countries, the United States and South America," she said, attributing the growing interest to a combination of "push and pull" factors.
In developed economies, sluggish growth and rising inflation have prompted more professionals to seek opportunities abroad, Wickertsheim explained. Layoffs at major technology companies have also driven skilled workers to explore other job markets, she added.
Meanwhile, professionals from countries such as those in South America admire China's rapid development and robust business ecosystem and hope to achieve joint growth with China, said Wickertsheim.
Wickertsheim noted that emerging industries such as biotechnology, pharmaceuticals and industrial automation are becoming increasingly important to her firm's recruitment business, while intelligent factories and robotic automation are emerging as key business areas.
Miriam Wickertsheim, general manager of recruitment firm Direct HR, speaks about legal and HR updates for international companies in China at an event in Shanghai, east China, Feb. 25, 2026. (Xinhua)
Beyond career prospects, social media is also reshaping perceptions of China, Wickertsheim said. While Western media coverage of China has often focused on controversies, the country's 30-day visa-free entry policy has enhanced its appeal to foreign visitors, who share real, positive personal experiences online, she said.
"People saw China's safe, clean, modern environment, friendly locals and delicious food," she said, adding that these positive impressions have become another key factor drawing international talent to the country.
PULL OF INNOVATION
China's fast-growing emerging industries, from artificial intelligence and robotics to new energy, are strengthening the pull of innovation, offering international professionals opportunities to put their expertise into practice.
Cao Jun, chief financial officer of Hydrexia, a Chinese hydrogen energy company, said a major strength of Chinese technology enterprises lies in their ability to closely integrate technological innovation, product manufacturing and practical applications.
In the hydrogen energy sector, China's relatively complete industrial chain and strong engineering and manufacturing capabilities allow international professionals to participate in every stage, from research and development to manufacturing and commercialization in overseas markets, Cao said.
China's push for innovation-driven growth extends across its economy. In the first half of 2026, the country's GDP grew 4.7 percent year-on-year, with new growth drivers, including high-end manufacturing, the digital economy and modern services, contributing more than 40 percent to economic growth, official data showed.
China last week issued guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces, calling for measures like closer integration of technological and industrial innovation and improved talent development mechanisms.
Such industrial policies also offer clues to where China's economy is headed. "The best industry development reference for foreign businesses and jobseekers comes from China's five-year development plans, which outline the country's investment priorities and emerging track directions," Wickertsheim said.
"More global enterprise executives and board members are now proactively learning about China's industrial policies, unlike in the past," she said. "This improved understanding helps foreign companies formulate more scientific China market strategies."
Hamza Boukili (L), founder of Shanghai Yunsuan Tech Company, talks to young entrepreneurs during the 2026 World AI Conference in Shanghai, east China, July 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Xiang)
OPPORTUNITIES BEYOND BORDERS
Hydrexia has expanded into overseas markets including the United States, Australia and Southeast Asia, building international teams that bring together employees familiar with Chinese technology and manufacturing as well as those with expertise in local markets.
Cao said the company aims to develop overseas teams that can serve local customers over the long term and become part of local hydrogen energy industries, rather than merely act as sales outlets for Chinese products.
Hydrexia employs about 250 people worldwide, with overseas business teams accounting for around 10 percent of its workforce. It plans to strengthen overseas teams over the next two to three years.
By the end of 2025, Chinese investors had established more than 50,000 overseas enterprises across 190 countries and regions, with China's cumulative outbound investment ranking among the world's top three for nine consecutive years. Chinese companies operating abroad have created an average of over 2 million jobs annually, according to the Ministry of Commerce.
China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for improving support services for enterprises operating overseas and encouraging eligible companies to carry out mutually beneficial overseas investment cooperation.
Wickertsheim said Direct HR has received increased inquiries from Chinese companies planning to expand overseas. She expects Chinese multinational enterprises to generate substantial demand for overseas recruitment over the next five years.

item.title: How excavators from China's inland city reach global markets smarter and faster
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18
NANNING, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- Two clicks ring out as a robot precisely positions a tightening tool over a bolt on an electric excavator and secures it in place. Every 12.5 minutes, another bright-green excavator rolls off the assembly line, ready to be shipped to markets around the world.
The scene unfolds at the LiuGong Excavator Intelligent Factory in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. Guangxi Liugong Machinery Co., Ltd., a leading Chinese machinery manufacturer, now offers over 100 electric product models, which are sold in more than 60 countries and regions.
LiuGong is headquartered in Liuzhou City, an inland industrial city in Guangxi. Built on a strong foundation in automobile manufacturing, steel and machinery, the city has been accelerating the digital and intelligent transformation of its traditional industries.
LiuGong's Excavator Intelligent Factory began operation in November 2023. Inside the bustling workshop, automated guided vehicles (AGVs) carrying components of various sizes glide through the aisles, delivering them to workstations where workers have placed orders.
For Zhao Qifeng, production manager at the factory's assembly line, one of the toughest challenges addressed by intelligent transformation is product inspection.
"Previously, workers used steel rulers, tape measures and stopwatches to carry out tests. Nowadays, we can obtain key parameters through an AI-powered robotic system in about 10 minutes," Zhao said. The resulting "health report" for each excavator is then uploaded to the company's digital system.
With an annual production capacity of more than 20,000 excavators, the factory has achieved an automation rate of 65 percent through its smart upgrade. Overall production capacity has increased by 45 percent, order response time has been cut by 45 percent, and production efficiency has improved by 25 percent.
In the first half of this year, LiuGong's overseas revenue exceeded 10 billion yuan (about 1.49 billion U.S. dollars) for the first time, up more than 20 percent year-on-year, according to Liu Shuangfeng, director of business operations at the company's international business division. LiuGong's footprint now extends to 180 countries and regions worldwide.
Liu said that the company's connection with global markets is expected to improve further thanks to the Pinglu Canal, which just opened to navigation in September.
The 134.2-kilometer canal links Guangxi's capital Nanning with the Beibu Gulf, opening to sea at Guangxi's Qinzhou Port. The closest maritime outlet for much of southwest China is also offering companies in Liuzhou a more efficient export route.
LiuGong plans to increase exports through Qinzhou Port, where more ocean-going vessels are expected to call following the opening of the new canal, according to Liu.
"Compared with shipping through ports in Guangdong, the route via Qinzhou can reduce the company's inland transportation costs by around 15 to 18 percent and shorten transit times by seven to 10 days," he said.
With an established railway network, Liuzhou now features two access routes to the sea: goods can either travel by rail directly to Qinzhou Port, or by rail to Nanning, where they can then reach the port at Beibu Gulf via the Pinglu Canal.
The routes complement each other, giving businesses more options and helping strengthen supply chain resilience, said Qi Jianfeng, director of the development and reform bureau of Liunan District, where Liuzhou Railway Port lies.
To speed up export procedures, a customs-supervised facility at the railway port conducted its first rail-sea intermodal transport customs clearance in May, allowing exporters to complete customs procedures in Liuzhou, said Luo Qiaofeng, chief of Liuzhou Customs.
By streamlining declaration, inspection and release procedures, Liuzhou's new one-stop clearance process has cut customs clearance time by about 48 hours per shipment. A digital system also enables automated checks of container and seal numbers, speeding up cargo release, Luo added.
Liuzhou's official data shows that the city's railway port handled 17,000 TEUs from January to September this year, 22 times the total for all of 2025.
Both the Pinglu Canal and Liuzhou Railway Port are part of China's efforts to develop the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, a trade route connecting China's inland regions with ASEAN and other global markets. The corridor is designated as one of China's strategic backbone passages in the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). Its construction is expected to be fully completed by 2035.
For Liuzhou, the corridor brings the city's increasingly smart manufacturing sector closer to the global market at a faster pace. Though the city lies inland, the sea is no longer that far away.
As Qi put it, "Liuzhou may not be by the sea, but the sea has always been in its people's hearts."

item.title: Xi's decades-long commitment to poverty reduction
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18
An aerial drone photo taken on Oct. 1, 2026 shows the Land Fingerprint Concert held in Dafang County of southwest China's Guizhou Province. (Xinhua/Yang Wenbin)
BEIJING, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- Poverty eradication is "a common ideal of humanity," Chinese President Xi Jinping has once said.
Five years after China declared a complete victory in the fight against absolute poverty in 2021, its approach continues to inspire poverty reduction efforts worldwide.
Xi's dedication to poverty alleviation spans decades, from his early work in poor rural communities to the nationwide campaign he led and his efforts to promote international cooperation -- a long-running endeavor that resonates as the world marks the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty on Saturday.
A DECADES-LONG PURSUIT
"A weak hatchling bird can be the first to fly, and the poorest can be the first to become rich," Xi wrote in a 1988 essay on the development of Ningde Prefecture in east China's Fujian Province.
The following summer, Xi, then Ningde's Party secretary, traveled by car and on foot to reach Xiadang, a remote mountain township that had no road access.
Xi returned to Xiadang twice, helping tackle problems with roads, electricity and water supplies. In 2019, residents wrote to tell him that their township had shaken off poverty, and he replied with congratulations.
After becoming China's top leader, Xi continued his hands-on approach to poverty reduction. He conducted more than 50 inspections and research visits related to poverty alleviation, traveling to all 14 of the country's contiguous areas of extreme poverty.
In February 2018, Xi visited impoverished Yi families in Zhaojue County, Sichuan Province, asking about their livelihoods and discussing ways to tackle poverty with villagers and local officials.
"Not a single ethnic group or family should be left behind in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects," he said during the visit.
On Feb. 25, 2021, Xi declared a "complete victory" in China's fight against absolute poverty. Over eight years, nearly 100 million rural residents had been lifted out of absolute poverty, enabling the country to meet the poverty reduction target of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development a decade ahead of schedule.
In a congratulatory letter to Xi, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the achievement "a reason for hope and inspiration to the entire community of nations."
An aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 11, 2026 shows a livestock-photovoltaic integration project in Yuanyi Village, Minning Town, Yongning County of Yinchuan, northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Yang Zhisen)
LESSONS BEYOND BORDERS
China's poverty reduction experience has attracted attention from leaders around the world, some of whom have sought inspiration from Xi's writings and visited places where his ideas were put into practice.
Xi's early ideas on poverty reduction and economic development were collected in "Up and Out of Poverty," a collection of speeches, articles and interviews from 1988 to 1990 during his tenure in Ningde. Explaining the title, Xi wrote that its significance lay first and foremost in uprooting the "poverty mentality" and "poverty thinking."
In a foreword to the book's Uzbek edition published in 2023, President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev said the work remained an important source of guidance for state and social governance more than three decades after its initial publication.
During his visit to China this month, President of Botswana Duma Gideon Boko traveled to Fuzhou and Ningde in Fujian Province, where Xi once worked, and visited an exhibition on poverty reduction. During talks with Xi in Beijing, Boko depicted China's development as "an economic and political miracle never seen in history."
In June 2018, Bounnhang Vorachith, then President of Laos, visited Shibadong Village in central China's Hunan Province to learn about China's approach to poverty reduction. In villager Shi Basan's home, he paused before a photograph showing Xi chatting with her beside a fire pit.
During that November 2013 visit, Xi first proposed "targeted poverty alleviation" in a discussion with villagers, calling for measures tailored to local conditions and each household's needs.
After retracing Xi's route and speaking with residents, Bounnhang voiced hope of bringing the village's experience back to Laos. In reply to a letter from the villagers the following year, he praised Shibadong's success as offering invaluable lessons for his country.
In September 2026, Prime Minister of Madagascar Mamitiana Rajaonarison also visited Shibadong, where he witnessed first-hand residents' changing lives and watched demonstrations of traditional Miao ethnic embroidery. He said the visit shown him Xi's deep concern for the people and provided inspiration for Madagascar.
Staff work at a winery of Minning Town, Yongning County in Yinchuan, northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, Oct. 14, 2025. (Xinhua/Wang Peng)
TURNING EXPERIENCE INTO ACTION
Xi's efforts to share China's poverty reduction experience abroad date back to his early tenure in Fujian Province.
There, he promoted Juncao technology as part of Fujian's poverty reduction cooperation with northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. In 2000, he introduced the technology to a visiting governor from Papua New Guinea and later helped establish a China-aided Juncao demonstration base in the Pacific island country.
Juncao technology uses grass to cultivate mushrooms and provide livestock feed. The technology has spread to more than 100 countries, creating hundreds of thousands of jobs.
In Zimbabwe, farmer Mandiudza Masvongo has earned 330 U.S. dollars from selling mushrooms since taking up Juncao cultivation in June 2025. The proceeds have helped her start a small cleaning products business, which she said could mark a turning point in her life.
Beyond agriculture, China's development assistance has also improved basic services and created opportunities for small businesses. In Cambodia's Tanorn village, a China-aided project brought better roads, clean water and solar power. Por Sokhim, once dependent on rice farming, now runs a grocery store, while her husband operates a motorcycle repair shop.
In 2021, Xi proposed the Global Development Initiative, with poverty reduction and food security among its priorities. In the five years since its launch, cooperation projects under the initiative have taken root and delivered tangible results in more than 120 countries.
At the 2024 G20 summit in Rio de Janeiro, Xi drew upon China's experience to express confidence in the prospects for poverty reduction across the developing world.
"If China can make it, other developing countries can make it too. This is what China's battle against poverty says to the world," he told world leaders.

item.title: The Long March: Half a Quilt
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
In November 1934, three female Red Army soldiers sheltered at villager Xu Jiexiu's home during the Long March. Seeing the impoverished family shivering without bedding, the soldiers cut their only marching quilt in half before departing: "When the revolution is won, we will bring you a new quilt."
Xu waited for 50 years. The elderly woman later said: "What is the Communist Party? They are the people who, even with just one quilt, will cut half of it off for the people."
Torn in two was a quilt; woven forever were the hearts of the people.

item.title: How can Ningxia wine make a lasting impression on the world?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
"We don't need to be like everybody else." At the 47th World Congress of Vine and Wine in Yinchuan, Ningxia, the OIV President highlighted the unique stories that China and Ningxia have to tell.
From the achievements of a young wine region to the terroir between the Helan Mountains and the Yellow River—and a memorable glass of Marselan—international guests shared what stood out to them about Ningxia. Their reflections point to a way forward: build on the region's strengths and let the world discover its distinctive wines.

item.title: Seepweed, birds turn Weihai shoreline into natural red wonderland
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
At the mouth of the Changyang River in Weihai, Shandong Province, east China, autumn has painted the coastline a striking red. Expanses of salt-tolerant seepweed carpet the tidal flats, drawing flocks of birds to this vibrant wetland.
